paragraphs.text: Camping can be an inexpensive holiday, but families new to it should start with a single night at a site close to home. This allows them to test their equipment and find out what they have forgotten.
Choose a tent that is larger than the number of people suggests. A four-person tent often has room only for four adults lying side by side, with no space for bags.
Sleeping mats are as important as sleeping bags. The ground takes heat from the body during the night, and even in summer campers can feel cold without insulation underneath.
Children usually enjoy camping more when they have jobs to do, such as collecting water or helping to put up the tent.
Always check the weather forecast before leaving, and pack waterproof clothing even if rain is not expected.
Many campsites also rent out equipment, which is a good way to try camping before buying a tent of your own.
